sam: Quick idea — can we standardize the client-side pagination surface across py/ts/go to a minimal continuation handshake? i.e. opaque continuation token + an optional resume(ctx) that returns an iterator. keep transports thin. thoughts?

nora: +1 for opaque token. ergonomic for app devs. main q: who owns retries for page fetches — SDK or transport?

mike: leaning transport. retries for idempotent page fetches are best handled where we know network semantics. pages are unary-ish. streaming fallback is the messy part.

anna: For streaming fallback we need an explicit resume API. re-playing pages by re-fetching offsets is brittle unless token carries offset/etag. resume(token) that yields pages feels clean.

ben: exposing resume(token) forces SDK to accept some sideband metadata (etag, last-seen-cursor) in the token. That adds parsing surface and compatibility issues across languages. Make token opaque to apps; transport can encode JSON/hex internally.

sam: Proposal sketch: ``client.listItems(req) -> PagedIterable``; ``PagedIterable.next()`` yields items; when a transient failure happens, we surface a RetryablePageError with an optional continuation token. Then apps can call ``PagedIterable.resume(token)`` or ``client.resumeList(token)``. token must be opaque string. transports free to embed whatever.

nora: We should standardize error classes/codes: RETRYABLE_PAGE_BREAK vs NON_RETRYABLE. otherwise consumer libs will keep duplicating heuristics. Also document backoff defaults (exp backoff with jitter, max 3 retries for page fetch).

devops-bot: :truck: deploy: canary sdk v0.23.4 -> test-runtimes (ci/build/4938)

mike: Cancellation semantics matter: cancellation token must propagate to transport layer so in-flight page fetches can be cancelled. Also per-page timeout > global timeout helps avoid a single stuck fetch stalling iterator.

anna: +1 on per-page deadline. Also think about resume idempotency: resume(token) semantics must guarantee at-least-once or exactly-once item delivery? probably at-least-once and document deduping expectations.

ben: Tests: add fuzzing for token corruption (mutated token should yield a defined ResumeTokenInvalid error). Also add cross-lang golden fixtures where transport embeds different shapes in token (json base64 vs proto).

sam: Tradeoffs recap: (1) opaque token keeps SDK surface small, (2) transport-owned retries centralize retry logic but SDK must expose Resume primitive, (3) need standardized error codes and small set of guarantees (at-least-once, per-page deadlines).

nora: Action: sam to draft a short follow-up RFC with API sketches + examples for py/ts/go. I'll own cross-lang test harness. target: end of sprint.

mike: Action: i'll prototype cancellation + per-page deadline in the runtime shim.

anna: Action: i'll write the resume/error doc blurb for docs site (include sample app patterns).

ben: Suggestion: include a tiny compatibility version in token header so we can evolve encoding without breaking clients. e.g. token = base64("v1|{...}").

sam: Good call. i'll include that in the draft. thanks all. :thumbsup:

nora: ack

mike: ack

# end of thread
